speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with fever and abdominal tenderness after giving birth. To better understand your condition, how many weeks postpartum are you, and how high has your temperature reached?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. You mentioned decreased bowel sounds and uterine tenderness; have you experienced any constipation, abdominal distension, or difficulty passing gas? Additionally, have you noticed any foul-smelling vaginal discharge or pain during urination?

REQUEST TEST: CBC, CRP, Urinalysis, and Serum HCG.
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of decreased bowel sounds, abdominal distension, and uterine tenderness strongly suggest a retained placental fragment or uterine atony causing peritonitis. I have requested an Abdominal X-Ray to look for free air or masses. Can you confirm if you have been passing flatus or stool since delivery, and does the pain worsen with movement?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Uncomplicated pregnancy leading up to a vaginal delivery. No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: Does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. Lives with her partner.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical picture of fever, uterine tenderness, and decreased bowel sounds post-vaginal delivery is concerning for a retained product of conception or uterine infection. Based on your history of an uncomplicated pregnancy and delivery, have you noticed any foul-smelling vaginal discharge or changes in the amount of bleeding since the procedure?

REQUEST TEST: Blood Culture, Pelvic Ultrasound.
REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: While we await the results of your blood culture and pelvic ultrasound, can you clarify the nature of your fever? Is it a persistent low-grade temperature or has it spiked to a high degree, and have you had any chills or rigors? Also, please confirm if the uterine tenderness is localized to the fundus or involves a broader area of the abdomen.

speaker: Patient
text: Complains of minor difficulty in breathing but denies any urinary pain, headache, vomiting, or diarrhea.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The new symptom of minor breathing difficulty is concerning; could you describe if the pain radiates to your shoulder or if you feel sharp pain when coughing? This will help determine if the uterine tenderness is associated with subcapsular liver rupture or free air under the diaphragm.

REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Tests, Amylase, Lipase.
REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Abelum.
